## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`requirement_proven` now returns `True` for an empty criteria list. That regression has to be fixed before merge, because a requirement with no criteria would be reported as proven.

## Changes
The pull request rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a sum of `proven` flags with the criteria count. It also adds a `reviewed_batch` helper that rejects empty batches, plus a new test module covering both functions.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — Restore the empty-criteria guard in requirement_proven — With `criteria=[]`, `sum(...)` is `0` and `len(criteria)` is `0`, so `0 == 0` returns `True`. The removed `bool(criteria) and ...` returned `False` for this input, and `tests/test_proof.py:6-8` never passes an empty list. — Requirements with no criteria are now reported as proven, which overstates proof status to anyone relying on this check. — Fix: Keep the base expression `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, or add an early `if not criteria: return False`, and extend `test_requirement_with_evidence` with an empty-list case.
